title: Epochal audit log retention and indexing recovery notes
content:
Purpose and summary:

This note collates operational guidance, implementation notes, and runbook fragments for our audit event storage lifecycle. It focuses on the epochal retention model weve been iterating on (hot/warm/cold epochs), index-level recovery and reindex/backfill approaches, and how those pieces integrate with RBAC v2, automated evidence collection, and downstream SIEM export. The intent is to be actionable for on-call engineers and engineers implementing next-phase pipeline improvements.

Scope:
- Applies to primary audit event stream (auth events, api-keys, routing decisions, admin actions, tenant-level configuration changes).
- Includes storage tiers (hot/warm/cold), indexing strategies, schema-migration considerations, and SIEM export behavior.
- Excludes end-user telemetry, metric time series (Prometheus), and internal debug traces unless explicitly annotated as audit evidence.

Design: epochal retention model (overview)
- Hot epoch: 0-30 days. Low-latency searchable indices, frequent compaction disabled, immediate SIEM export for critical events.
- Warm epoch: 31-180 days. Fewer replicas, index refresh rate relaxed, queries acceptable at slightly higher latency.
- Cold epoch: 181 days - retention end. Object store blobs (compressed, immutable), skeleton index for existence and pointers to archived blobs to enable evidence retrieval.
- Retention TTLs are configured per event class (e.g., authentication failures 365 days, admin actions 730 days, configuration change events 1095 days). These override the epoch defaults.

Indexing and partitioning strategy
- Use time-based indices with daily rollups for hot epoch. Index name pattern: audit-YYYY.MM.DD-v{schema}.
- Warm epoch compaction: consolidate daily indices into monthly indices to reduce shard count. Metadata about compaction is stored in the index metadata (compaction_version and source_indices).
- Cold epoch: data snapshotted to object storage (GCS) in ndjson.gz packs with accompanying manifest JSON describing first_seq_id, last_seq_id, checksum, schema_version, and originating index names. The index entry kept for cold is minimal: event_id, event_time, event_type, pointer_to_blob (gs://...), schema_version, evidence_tags (if present).

Schema evolution and RBAC v2 considerations
- Schema versioning: every write includes a schema_version and sequence_number. Migration is additive-first: new optional fields are introduced with default-null handling. Backwards compatibility is required for all active indices in hot/warm epochs.
- RBAC v2 metadata: events capturing RBAC decisions must include rbac_version, policy_id, decision, actor_id, and actor_role_snapshot. These fields are required for audit compliance.
- When migrating schema for RBAC v2 (e.g., adding role-hash field), plan a two-pass strategy: (1) accept writes with new fields while reading tolerant of old records, (2) run background normalizer to annotate older records in warm indices before compaction into monthly indices.

Evidence automation tagging
- Evidence-producing events (artifacts attached to audit records) must follow the evidence schema: evidence_id, storage_pointer, storage_checksum, collection_method, and integrity_proof. Evidence automation jobs write both the audit event and a separate immutable evidence manifest into object storage; audit index stores pointer and hash only.
- The evidence automation worker must write manifest using a transactional pattern: write manifest to GCS, confirm MD5/SHA checksum, then write audit event referencing manifest ID. If audit write fails, manifest is tombstoned and garbage-collected after a grace period.

SIEM export and downstream compatibility
- Critical events (policy violations, admin console changes, data exfiltration alarms) are forwarded in near real-time to SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle) via the export bridge. Exports carry schema_version and event_fingerprint to allow dedup and de-dup logic in SIEM.
- Export retries: the bridge tracks per-event attempt count; transient failures use exponential backoff with jitter; if export fails more than 5 times, escalate to incident channel and mark event with export_status:failed.

Backfill and reindex strategies (idempotent and observable)
- Principles: all operations must be idempotent, resumable, and emit progress to our backfill-tracking dashboard (Airflow/GCS-driven state).
- Small reindex (<14 days): run parallel workers keyed by day shards. Reindex job flow: snapshot source index -> transform (schema normalizer, RBAC enrichment) -> bulk index to target -> verify doc count, checksums -> swap alias.
- Large backfill (>14 days or cross-epoch): create manifest-driven batch jobs that read sequentially from snapshot blobs and write to new index format. The job writes a progress marker after every XMB processed so it can resume mid-blob without reprocessing earlier shards.
- De-dup strategy: use source_event_id as the external id when reindexing; bulk index with create-or-update semantics using primary key to deduplicate. Sequence numbers and event_fingerprint help detect divergent duplicates.

Failure modes and mitigation (operational runbook)
- Failure: partial index writes (some shards failed)
  - Symptom: doc_count mismatch vs expected; reindex progress stalled; increased search errors for a time window.
  - Action: pause alias swap; inspect job logs in backfill dashboard; if failed shards are transient, resubmit failed shard jobs; if corruption detected, mark index read-only and run verify-checksums across shards.

- Failure: missing evidence blobs referenced by index pointers
  - Symptom: evidence retrieval attempts return 404 or checksum mismatch during validation.
  - Action: check artifact tombstone queue; query evidence automation job logs; if manifest exists in tombstone, run automated restore from archival tier (if available) or trigger manual restore request to Compliance with retention justification. Raise incident if evidence lost for P0 audit.

- Failure: SIEM export backlog
  - Symptom: bridge lag exceeds 30m or retry-counts spike above threshold.
  - Action: scale bridge consumers temporarily, enable backpressure (pause non-critical exports), and open JIRA ticket for root-cause. If queue is irrecoverably unhealthy, snapshot backlog to GCS and process offline to prevent duplicate delivery.

- Failure: schema drift causing silent drops
  - Symptom: downstream consumers complain about missing fields; exporter logs show serialization failures for particular schema_version.
  - Action: revert exporter binary to previous stable version; kick off a corrective reindex for the impacted time range with a normalization transform to include expected fields. Add consumer-level contract tests to CI.

Monitoring, SLOs and alerting
- Ingestion lag SLO: 95th percentile ingestion-to-indexed latency <= 20s for hot epoch events. Alert if 95p > 60s for 10m.
- Reindex job health SLO: all scheduled backfills must make forward progress every 15m. Alert if job does not checkpoint for >30m.
- SIEM export SLO: 99% of marked-critical events forwarded within 120s. Alert on dropped exports or queue > 30k events.
- Evidence integrity SLO: manifests must match storage checksum on first retrieval; alert on integrity failures >0.01%.

Operational checklist (quick steps for common ops)
1) When starting a planned reindex, create a backfill JIRA with date ranges, schema_version target, and expected duration.
2) Reserve additional cluster capacity for the reindex window (scale up hot nodes or dedicated reindex pool).
3) Run a dry-run transform on a 24-hour snapshot and review diffs for field changes.
4) Execute reindex with conservative parallelism; monitor metrics (bulk throughput, rejected ops, queue length).
5) Validate doc counts and checksums; swap alias during low-traffic window; keep old index read-only for 72h before deletion.

Appendix: sample queries and checks
- Quick doc count: GET /_cat/indices/audit-2025.11.*?v
- Missing evidence pointer check: POST /audit/_search { query: { bool: { must: [ { exists: { field: "pointer_to_blob" } }, { bool: { must_not: { exists: { field: "evidence_checksum" } } } } ] } } }
- Verify manifest checksum: gsutil cat gs://audit-archives/2025-11-03/manifest-0001.json | jq -r '.checksum'

Open items and next steps:
- Automate monthly compaction job to run with a canary index and automated smoke tests.
- Add consumer contract tests for SIEM exporters to our CI pipeline.
- Formalize evidence tombstone and GC retention policy and publish SLA for retrieval during legal holds.
- Explore a low-cost cold-search option (vector index over compressed event summaries) to enable basic queries on cold epoch without full rehydration.

If youre oncall and get paged for any of the above P0 symptoms, follow the runbook above and ping the security-compliance rotation on Slack #sec-oncall. This doc should be considered living; propose edits as PRs against CONFLUENCE-SEC-233 (linked artifact).
